paragraphs.text: It was of God, then, that the people fell into such straits: that where human help failed, divine might come in. {a}
{a} Necesse est adesse divinum, ubi humanum cessat auxilium. - Philo Jud.
i.e., Return. In passing the Red Sea, the Israelites made a semicircle. Compare Exo 13:20 Num 33:8. God must be followed, though he lead us through a maze or labyrinth.
Perplexed; intricated; they know not what to do, or which way to turn. Enemies watch opportunities, but oft miss of their meaning.

By subduing this sturdy rebel, and bringing "his violent dealing upon his own pate." {Psa 7:16} When the prophet cried to Jeroboam’s altar, it clave presently asunder. {1Ki 13:2-3} But the mighty "hammer" of "God’s word," {Jer 23:29} with ten miracles, gave ten mighty strokes at Pharaoh’s heart, and yet could find no entrance. God will therefore now take another course with him.
i.e., Ran quite away, without any resolution ever to return. This troubled the tyrant. Crowns have their cares. Little David likes his hook the better ever since he saw the court.
To meet his destruction.
They fought of old out of chariots armed with scythes and hooks; which at first were a terror, and after a scorn. {a}
{a} Veget., lib. i. cap. 24.
Bravely; boldly; in battle array, not as runaways; in all comely equipage.
And God made fair way before them, till they came into the Red Sea.
Because sorely distressed.

They saw no way to escape, unless they could have gone up to heaven: which because they could not, heaven came down to them, though unworthy, that God might get him a name. {Isa 63:12; Isa 63:14} The Israelites herein were far more happy than those ancient Britons, who, being greatly distressed by their northern enemies in the time of Valentinian III, implored the aid of Aetius, the Roman prefect of Gaul, using these words: "To Aetius, thrice consul, the sighs of the Britons": and after thus they complain, "The barbarous enemy beats us to the sea; the sea beats us back to the enemy: between these two kinds of deaths, we are either murdered or drowned." {a} But their implorations prevailed not. Neither found they any other remedy than what the Prince of Orange showed to his soldiers at the battle of Newport; when they had the sea on one side and the Spaniards on the other. If, saith he, you will live, you must either eat up these Spaniards, or drink up this sea. {b}
{a} Daniel’s Chronicle.
{b} Hist. of Netherl.
Thus "they provoked him at the sea, at the Red Sea; nevertheless he saved them for his name’s sake." {Psa 106:7-8}
Invalidum omne natura querulum. {a} Weak spirits are ever quarrelling and contending.
{a} Seneca.
Thus God "heard their cry at the Red Sea," {Neh 9:9} though it were not the cry of faith, but of fright and perturbation. So he "heard the voice of the lad." {Gen 21:17}
paragraphs.anchor: Stand still, and see the salvation.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Ye shall neither say nor do.
so., With inward groanings, without any audible voice. Moses egit vocis silentio, ut corde clamaret. And God was readier to answer than he to ask.
q.d., There is something more to be done than to pray. Ora et labora. {a} We must not only crave God’s help, but be forward in the course whereby to make way for God’s help.
paragraphs.anchor: Speak unto the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Though upon a manifest danger. This is an act of strong faith, pure obedience.
{a} August.
This rod God makes use of, fo: the greater manifestation of his own power, and the gracing of his servant Moses.
paragraphs.anchor: But lift thou up thy rod.

paragraphs.text: See on Exo 9:35.

Made me "a name as at this day." {Neh 9:10} For this he was famous in far countries. Jethro, the first proselyte to the Jewish Church, was hereby converted, say the Rabbins. And the Philistines cry, "Woe unto us! these are the gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness." {1Sa 4:8}
paragraphs.anchor: When I have gotten me honour.

paragraphs.text: Christ, the Angel of God’s presence. See Exo 13:21; Exo 23:23.
So "the glory of the Lord" was "their rearward." {Isa 58:8} He will be to his both van and rear. {Isa 52:12}
{See Trapp on "Heb 12:2"}
paragraphs.anchor: A cloud and darkness to them.

paragraphs.text: Of that pseudo-Moses that cozened many credulous Jews of Crete into the midst of the sea, anno 434, see Funceius’s Chron. at that year.
paragraphs.anchor: And Moses stretched out his hand.

paragraphs.text: So was that torrent of fire, if Aristotle {a} may be believed, that ran from Etna, consuming the country, and yet parted itself; making a kind of a lane for those that ventured to rescue their aged parents.
{a} De Mundo, cap. 6.
Every main affliction is our Red Sea, saith one, which, while it threats to swallow, preserves us.

God permitting it, and making fair weather before them, they also blustering, and "breathing out threatenings," saying, "I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil," &c., till anon "they sank as lead in the mighty waters." {Exo 15:9-10}

God "watcheth upon the evil to bring it" upon his enemies then when he may do them a greatest mischief. {Dan 9:14} He picketh his times for vengeance: "Now will I rise, saith the Lord; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself." {Isa 33:10}

He set his eyes upon them; as Paul did upon Elymus the sorcerer; with highest offence, and utmost indignation. After which lightning follows that terrible thunderclap, wherewith he troubled them and took off their wheels. See Psa 77:18-19; Psa 18:15.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord looked unto the host.

paragraphs.text: By wind that God sent. {Exo 15:10} "The winds blow, the waters flow." {Psa 147:18}
paragraphs.anchor: That the waters may come again.

paragraphs.text: For by being divided, it had been weakened. Si collidimur, frangimur. The daughter of dissension is dissolution.
No more doth there of our subdued iniquities. {Mic 7:10} Peccata non redeunt. We shall see them no more, any otherwise than these Israelites did their enemies, dead upon the shore.
paragraphs.anchor: There remained not so much as one of them.

paragraphs.text: This is applied as a type of Christ, {1Co 10:2} to show that Christ is present with his people, to save them in all troubles and afflictions, {Isa 43:2} and from all their spiritual enemies and sins, both by justification and sanctification, {Mic 7:19} through faith in him, {Heb 11:29} and will in the end give them songs of victory and triumph. {Exo 15:1-27: 1Ki 15:3}
paragraphs.anchor: But the children of Israel walked upon dry land.

paragraphs.text: A mercy never enough memorised. What, then, is our redemption from sin, death, and hell
